shipped_rows.title_o: Attention control, memory updating, and emotion regulation temporarily reduce the capacity for executive control.

blind_target.authors: Healey MK, Hasher L, Danilova E
blind_target.title: The stability of working memory: Do previous tasks influence complex span?
blind_target.evidence_quote:
In this study, for the depletion task, we used the actual video material and verbatim instructions from the popular video-viewing attention control task employed by prior researchers. For the outcome task, we used a complex working memory span task known as the operation span task (OSPAN; [
36
]). We selected these particular tasks because they maximize the chances of demonstrating the ego-depletion effect for the following reasons: a) the video-viewing attention control task is one of the most widely used tasks and has consistently been shown to induce ego-depletion in prior research (e.g., [
5
,
31
–
33
]); b) the OSPAN task places heavy demand on executive attention and hence should tax self-control resources (e.g., [
37
]); c) this particular combination of tasks has produced medium to large effect sizes in prior studies [
5
,
38
]; d) these tasks are matched in terms of stimulus modality (i.e., both tasks utilize words), which has been shown to amplify the ego-depletion effect [
38
].
blind_target.outcome_quote: Contrary to the ego-depletion hypothesis, participants in the depletion condition did not perform worse than control participants on the subsequent self-control task, even after considering moderator variables.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The task combination is explicitly linked to these two prior effect demonstrations; the present attempt finds no depletion effect.

luna_triage.reason: Healey, Hasher, and Danilova (2011) is cited as prior work supporting the use of this particular combination of video-viewing and OSPAN tasks; the source does not retest Healey et al.'s specific finding about whether previous tasks influence complex-span performance. Its stated goal is a broader test of the ego-depletion effect. Shipped row 1665 is Schmeichel (2007), another prior task study, not a match for Healey.
luna_triage.location: Introduction statement of goals; Methods task description; References 38.
luna_triage.omission_quote: We had two primary goals in conducting this research. The first goal (represented by Hypothesis 1 below) was to attempt to replicate the ego-depletion effect as it is typically demonstrated in the existing literature but with a much larger sample size.
